# Summary section (sample close-out, same source as workflow_state.json; 2026-10-09)

## Materials and objective
- Sample: amorphous carbon anode (stated by the user), Rigaku data `pattern_2theta.txt` (RAW4.00 ASCII, 3432 points, 10–80°, step 0.0204°, 40 kV/40 mA, 2026-09-23); the same directory's `pattern.raw` (binary RAW1.01) is archived and unused (not readable by the plugin).
- λ facts: Cu doublet Kα1=1.5406 / Kα2=1.54439 / ratio=0.5, source = RAW header (Anode=Cu; Monochromator=0 ⇒ Kα2 not stripped, ActuallyUsedLambda=1.5418 is the Kα average and must not be taken as monochromatic), passed explicitly into all 4 fitting rounds.
- Objective (same sentence as the goal): fit the main broad humps of category-C amorphous material to an R plateau with the bounded manual engine (reference target Rwp < ≈10%, not a hard threshold); output the broad-hump peak positions/d, the Scherrer apparent size (with protocol), impurity screening, the figure and the report; the products are stored in this directory. **Result: achieved (Rwp=3.81%, χ²=1.06).**

## Phases and crystal families (conclusion + basis + excluded families and why)
- Conclusion: **no crystalline phase** (no sharp Bragg peak in the full pattern); the main body is the diffuse scattering of amorphous/turbostratic carbon, described by 3 empirical broad humps:
  - ex2: 16.506±0.050°, d=5.366 Å, FWHM 7.55°, pure Gaussian (η frozen at 0) — low-angle porosity / expanded interlayer correlation scattering (typical of amorphous carbon);
  - ex0: 29.942±0.061°, d=2.982 Å, FWHM 11.84°, pure Lorentzian (η frozen at 1) — main diffuse band (interlayer-type correlation of strongly disordered sp2 clusters; d is clearly smaller than graphite's 3.35 Å, indicating strongly turbostratic/bent/compressed stacking, not graphite long-range order);
  - ex1: 42.132±0.041°, d=2.143 Å, FWHM 6.80°, η=0.574±0.142 — in-plane (100)-type C–C correlation (graphite d100=2.13 Å, assignment robust).
- Basis: V1 image reading (broad humps, no sharp peaks) + 4 rounds of residual binning (all systematic residuals cleared) + residual z scan (0 points >4σ) + residual peak picking (all 40 peaks at 12–28 counts ≈ the noise rms of 27.7).
- Families excluded and why: graphite/microcrystalline graphite (no sharp (002) at 26.5°, no (101)/(004) series); crystalline impurity phases such as Cu/Al current-collector foil (no sharp peak at any of 38.5/43.3/44.7/50.4/65.1/74.1°); nanocrystalline Si/Sn/SiO₂ etc. (no corresponding multi-peak series, the residual has no unexplained sharp peak). The category-C workflow skips the phase-identification stage per the skill (no sharp impurity ⇒ fit the main body directly).

## Defect master table (exhaustive → screening → execution)
- Not applicable: this sample is **amorphous** (no lattice ⇒ the 14 classes of crystal defects in Appendix A have no host structure); no defect_table.json was built. The "defect" information of the amorphous system (porosity, turbostratic stacking, sp2/sp3 ratio) is already contained in the empirical broad-hump decomposition (ex2 porosity component, ex0 turbostratic main band). None of the trigger conditions of the complex-situation checklist occurred: no manual-fitting-failure input, no 3 consecutive rounds without improvement (no_improve_streak=1, caused by closing Round4 with the same model as Round3), no unexplained residual structure.

## Achieved results (R and protocol written separately; FullProf Rwp and GSAS wR are not directly comparable)
- **Manual engine (bounded LM, Poisson-weighted) protocol**: Rwp=3.808%, Rexp=3.702%, χ²=1.058, GOF≈1.03; baseline (starting parameters) Rwp=95.30%. fit_status entirely clean (success, no max_nfev, no bound hitting, covariance complete); r_plateau=true (this model + data are exhausted in this engine). Trajectory: 6.174 → 4.312 → 3.808 → 3.808 (journal.jsonl is authoritative).
- FullProf/fp2k not used (no crystal structure to convert into a pcr), GSAS-II not used (Rietveld does not apply to an amorphous material; the components source is exactly the output protocol specified by the plugin) — the two protocols' numbers do not exist for this sample, so there is no cross-protocol comparison issue.
- Scherrer apparent coherence length (**instrumental broadening not subtracted = apparent value**, K=0.9, λ=1.5406, Kα2 not stripped): main broad hump 29.75°/FWHM4.48° → **D≈1.84 nm**; 41.30°/FWHM3.19° → **D≈2.66 nm** (the protocol as directly measured by the tool). Model dependence disclosed: converted from the fitted component widths it is 0.69–1.25 nm (in the empirical decomposition ex0 also serves as the diffuse base, and the width protocol differs). Robust conclusion: **coherence domain of order ~1–2 nm (roughly 2–6 graphene layers), no long-range crystalline order**, consistent with "amorphous carbon".
- Band area fractions (semi-quantitative, RIR/density/absorption not divided out, used only as diffuse-scattering apportionment): ex0 74.8% / ex1 12.6% / ex2 12.7%. **Crystallinity cannot be given**: there is no crystalline phase reference, and all scattering is diffuse.

## Not tried · undecided items
- Not tried (with reasons): GSAS-II/fp2k (an amorphous material has no structure model, not applicable); bg_scan background escalation (χ²≈1.06 has already reached the statistical limit and the target is achieved, escalation would only overfit the noise); peak cutting cut (the gate was not triggered: no current-collector/artifact peak); Williamson-Hall strain separation (a deliberate boundary of the plugin, and meaningless for amorphous broad humps); synchrotron/neutron total-scattering PDF analysis (beyond what this data can support).
- Undecided (requires the user / supplementary characterization): the synthesis route and precursor are unknown (this affects the depth of the physical interpretation of the ex2 porosity component and the ex0 turbostratic degree); no Raman (sp2/sp3, D/G ratio are the key characterizations complementary to XRD); no XPS/TEM/specific surface area (porosity and surface-chemistry evidence); the main band d=2.98 Å is smaller than the typical hard-carbon (002) 3.3–3.6 Å — if the assignment (strongly bent graphene clusters vs mixed phases) needs to be investigated further, supplementary Raman/TEM is recommended.
- "Not tried" and "tried but ineffective" are kept separate: all the "not tried" items above are **not applicable / unnecessary**, and there is no "tried but ineffective" item (all 4 rounds improved monotonically or closed out level).

## Handover recommendations
- If continuing: ① after adding Raman, compare the D/G and sp2/sp3 with the band areas/widths of this fit; ② if trace crystalline impurities (<1%) are suspected, re-measure with a longer counting time or use synchrotron radiation, then redo the residual screening (the detection limit here ≈ noise level, 12–28 counts); ③ an empirical broad-hump decomposition carries an inherent model dependence (number of components/shape family), so when comparing across samples **the same decomposition protocol must be fixed**; ④ keep the comments on the two edits of the engine copy `xrd_engine_custom.py` (H upper bound 15, η refinable in [0,1]) when reusing it.
- Deliverables: `report.md`, `round4_final_fit.png`, `result_round4_final.json`, `components_round4_final.json`, `plan_round4_final.json`, and this journal directory.
